entries.claim: Redaction now runs only on `messages[*].content`; the later `response_format` insertion is never passed through `egress::for_destination`, so any secret-like literal embedded in a schema or other top-level request scaffold now reaches the wire unfiltered. The previous whole-body redaction covered this path.
entries.failure_scenario: A caller configures `response_format` with a JSON schema whose description, example, or default contains a secret token or auth-looking string; that literal is serialized verbatim into the provider request instead of being redacted.

counter_evidence.note: The exclusion is this phase CONTEXT decision D-07 (.planning/phases/2/CONTEXT.md:98), and the code states the evidence for it inline: `model`, `response_format` and the caller `json_schema` are not transcript text, and a schema property name coming back `[redacted]` inside `response_format` is the 400 the 2026-08-21 DeepSeek probe recorded. The schema is supplied by this crate own caller, not carried in from a user transcript, so it is not a path user secrets arrive on. The finding asks for the alternative D-07 rejected on recorded evidence, which is an approach difference rather than a defect.

entries.claim: `the_filtered_body_is_the_same_document_with_different_values` does not actually check that filtering changed any value; it only compares shape (message count, roles, top-level key order). If the redaction call were removed entirely, this test would still pass because the body layout stays the same.
entries.failure_scenario: A regression makes `egress::for_destination` a no-op on message content; the request is still valid JSON with the same keys and roles, so this test remains green and misses the leak.
